assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established liquid-liquid phase separation as a general physical-chemical principle for organising cell interiors without membranes. It brings polymer physics, phase behaviour and multivalent interactions into cell biology, which is the kind of concept-forming discovery I value most. The importance is high across biology, medicine (condensate disorders, amyloid-like transitions) and soft-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 P-granule work (Brangwynne, Hyman) is the decisive demonstration; Rosen's multivalent-interaction phase diagrams give the quantitative physical-chemical basis. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded grammar and are significant but could be left out of a three-person prize. Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen look like the most defensible trio, though the allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in hundreds of systems and well established as a concept, and now more than 15 years old. The timing is fair, but the debate over how far in vitro droplets reflect in vivo condensates is still active.
uncertainties: Physiological relevance and functional versus pathological roles of many reported condensates remain debated.
Whether the prize would be judged chemistry rather than physiology or medicine; I cannot verify how the Academy would weigh this.
Rosen versus Pappu or Mittag as third laureate is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view of protein folding resolved Levinthal's paradox and turned folding into a statistical-mechanical problem. It is a thermodynamic, physical-chemistry concept that unifies folding, misfolding, aggregation and later computational structure work. Originality and conceptual clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes with Bryngelson laid down the theory, and Onuchic and Wolynes developed the funnel picture. Dill's hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model work is a parallel, partly different line of credit. Fersht's experimental mapping is a separate contribution. Wolynes and Onuchic are the core, and Dill is the plausible third. Bryngelson's early role makes a clean configuration contentious.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation through experiment (phi-value analysis), simulation and its influence on structure-based prediction. It is mature and arguably overdue, but the concept is partly absorbed into textbook knowledge, which can blur the sense of a single discovery.
uncertainties: Credit split between Wolynes/Onuchic, Dill, Bryngelson and Fersht's experimental line.
Recent AI structure prediction may crowd the narrative, and the Academy has already recognised computation and protein structure in 2024; I cannot verify how it would weigh this.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry behind siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines. The work rests on lipid self-assembly, pKa-dependent charge and membrane fusion, which is physical chemistry I know well. The practical impact on medicine is large and demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) developed the lipid-particle formulation and ionizable-lipid principles; Anderson and Langer contributed lipid libraries and optimised materials. The group is large and the credit is intertwined, so choosing three is difficult. My proposed trio is a reasonable but contestable choice.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale (Onpattro, COVID-19 mRNA vaccines), with independent confirmation. Recognition would be timely, and the 2023 Medicine prize on mRNA modification leaves the delivery side open.
uncertainties: Whether Cullis, Anderson or Langer holds the strongest claim to the key ionizable-lipid step; I cannot verify the detailed priority record.
Patent disputes and company histories may complicate attribution.
The fit for a chemistry versus a medicine or engineering prize is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues created a new therapeutic modality based on induced proximity, and the mechanism of thalidomide-type glues was a striking chemical-biology discovery. The idea is original, clear and clinically consequential.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains the glue mechanism. Ciulli, Gray and others made major later advances. A trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa spans the two strands but leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials, but approval of a PROTAC-based drug is still pending as far as I know. Scientific confirmation is broad, though the clinical verdict is not yet in, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical outcome is not yet decided.
The two strands (PROTACs and molecular glues) may need separate credit.
Credit for Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray and Ito is not accommodated in a trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another through chemistry on DNA without double-strand breaks, extending genome editing to precise single-nucleotide changes. It is a clear chemical-biology invention with growing therapeutic use and wide research impact.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory made the key inventions, with Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors) as lead authors. Kondo and Nishida independently reported a deaminase-based editor, and that parallel work complicates credit. Liu alone would be the cleanest option, but the supplied names permit a fair trio.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and in clinical trials, including early patient treatments. It is rapidly maturing, and recognition would be timely, though the 2020 CRISPR prize makes it a follow-on.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 prize and with B043 (prime editing), which shares a principal.
Priority of the Kondo/Nishida work relative to Komor and Gaudelli.
Long-term safety and off-target profile are still under study.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami demonstrated programmable self-assembly of arbitrary nanoscale shapes from base-pairing rules. It is a strong example of a molecular-organisation concept, and it has become a design platform for nanomachines, sensing and templating.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami paper is the decisive step. Seeman, the founder of DNA nanotechnology, is not in the credited names, and the Academy might see that as a gap in credit. Winfree and Yan contributed algorithmic assembly and 2D/3D structures, while Shih and Yin developed 3D origami and tile-based methods. The configuration is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a method with wide independent use, but real-world applications beyond research tools are still emerging. The impact is more as a design concept than as a deployed technology.
uncertainties: Seeman's absence from the credited names weakens a fair allocation.
Which of Winfree, Yan, Shih and Yin is the most decisive besides Rothemund.
Practical impact is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages and capsules showed how coordination thermodynamics and reversibility give precisely defined hollow architectures, with host-guest chemistry, catalysis and confined-space reactivity. It is a clear and original chemical concept for molecular organisation.
assessment.attribution: Fujita (the first self-assembled M6L4 cages), Raymond (tetrahedral and other cage assemblies, confined catalysis) and Stang (supramolecular coordination macrocycles and polyhedra) are the senior pioneers. Nitschke and Ward are important later contributors. The trio of Fujita, Raymond and Stang is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and broad adoption. Timely, though the 2016 and 1987 supramolecular prizes mean the Academy could view it as a continuation of a recognised area.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier supramolecular and molecular-machine prizes.
Application impact is moderate compared with other candidates.
Credit among Fujita, Raymond, Stang, Nitschke and Ward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dye-sensitised nanocrystalline solar cells introduced a mesoporous-electrode and molecular-sensitiser design for photovoltaics, with an interfacial electron-transfer and kinetics picture that is solid physical chemistry. It opened a field and later seeded perovskite solar cells.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel paper is the decisive step, with Grätzel the intellectual leader. Hagfeldt contributed later mechanistic and efficiency work. A one- or two-person configuration is clean and fair.
assessment.maturity: Over 30 years of replication, with commercial niche use. The record is secure, but efficiency never rivalled silicon, so the sense of lasting impact is mixed, and halide perovskites may have taken attention.
uncertainties: Commercial and efficiency impact has been limited.
Possible competition with the perovskite candidate for the same narrative.
I cannot verify the exact attribution split between O'Regan and Grätzel.
